business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Multi-Axis Computerized Numerical Control Metal Centers

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law with Islamic Sharia principles)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement on Promotion, Protection and Guarantee of Investments among Arab States (1980)
Egypt–United Kingdom Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (1977, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 7 of 2020; Executive Regulations dated 2003, as revised; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 148 of 2020); GAFI Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Disclosure Rules issued under the Investment Law (2021); Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Regulations, including Circular No. 13 of 2020 as updated.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (final draft, Arabic and English)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the incorporator's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (Egypt is a Hague Apostille Convention party since 14 December 2021)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the local incorporation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of shareholders' resolution authorizing incorporation and UBO statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary / board of directors of the foreign applicant

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incorporation of the corporate shareholder (if any)
Bank reference letter and AML/KYC 'Know Your Customer' certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy; apostille not mandatory for banking correspondence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and senior managers against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the domestic Egyptian designations published by the Central Bank of Egypt and the Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Unit. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs and any individual or entity linked to high-risk jurisdictions. Screening must be repeated at incorporation and at least annually thereafter, or upon any material ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Investor Registration Portal / e-services platform; final clearance confirmed through the Commercial Registry Directorate of the Ministry of Justice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All company names must be denominated in Arabic. An English transliteration or a complementary English name may be registered provided the Arabic name is the presiding legal designation. Names containing religious, political, military, or government-referencing terms are prohibited without express ministerial consent. The name must also avoid any false indication of a regulated activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Islamic (when used in a manner implying official religious character)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The GAFI name reservation certificate is valid for 180 days and may be extended for an additional 180 days upon submission of a written extension request before the expiry date. In the event of rejection, the applicant may file an administrative grievance with the GAFI Grievance Committee within 30 days of the rejection notice. If the grievance is dismissed, the applicant may initiate an appeal before the Administrative Judiciary at the State Council (Consell d'État), subject to applicable procedural deadlines.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for industrial manufacturing activities under ISIC 2822. The LLC must maintain a physical registered office in Egypt and a separate factory/industrial premises approved by the Industrial Development Authority (IDA). A virtual office or a service-only address will be rejected by GAFI and the Commercial Registry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: estimated >75% probability of unannounced physical inspection of both the registered office and the factory site by GAFI and the Industrial Development Authority within the first 12 months of operation, due to the precision CNC machine tool manufacturing license conditions and higher AML risk classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Egyptian Companies Law, as amended) Articles 1, 26, and 89; the executive regulation promulgated by Ministerial Decree No. 420 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017) governing GAFI one-stop-shop incorporation of Limited Liability Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department and Investor One-Stop Shop at the registered office jurisdiction; commercial registration notification is made through GAFI to the local Commercial Registry office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association (عقد التأسيس) and Articles of Association (النظام الأساسي) for a Limited Liability Company, submitted through the GAFI electronic incorporation portal, entered into the Commercial Registry (السجل التجاري), and published in the Egyptian Official Bulletin (الوقائع المصرية).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Egyptian LLC; the founding shareholders fix the share capital in the Memorandum of Association. All subscribed capital must be fully paid and placed in an escrow / blocked account opened in the company name with an Egyptian bank before incorporation, and the bank's capital deposit certificate (شهادة إيداع رأس المال) must accompany the GAFI filing. Inward remittances by foreign shareholders require the bank exchange certificate (Statement MI/19); locked funds are released only after the Commercial Registration certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST, that each founding shareholder subscribes in full to the ordinary share capital allocated in Schedule A of the Memorandum of Association, and that such capital be deposited in the company's escrow account prior to GAFI incorporation filing. RESOLVED SECOND, that the registered office of the Company within Egypt be adopted at the address set out in the Memorandum of Association and that the General Manager be authorized to complete the Commercial Registry notification. RESOLVED THIRD, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed General Manager, and [Name] be appointed secretary and principal signatory, with full authority to submit incorporation documents and open bank accounts. RESOLVED FOURTH, that all costs of formation be borne and ratified by the shareholders, and the General Manager shall take every further action to obtain the industrial operating license.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Name Clearance, and Founders' Pre-Incorporation Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI electronic services portal and the local Notary Public (الشهر العقاري) in the intended governorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an Arabic-language name search through the GAFI online system; submit three ranked proposed Arabic names with English transliterations; obtain the negative-name certificate (شهادة عدم تعارض الاسم) before drafting the Memorandum; execute the first Shareholders' / Board resolution appointing the formation agent; begin preparation of the bank escrow instruction.
required_dossiers: GAFI name search application form (prescribed template)
Three proposed Arabic names and Latin transliteration versions
Copy of national ID or passport for each founding shareholder
Founders' preliminary incorporation resolution
Notarized Power of Attorney where formation is delegated to an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts, the applicant may petition the GAFI Legal Affairs Office within 15 days for reconsideration or elect the next priority alternative name without additional filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Notarization of the Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved Egyptian commercial bank in the registered office area and the Notary Public office (electronic notarization channel linked to GAFI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the escrow / blocked bank account in the intended company name, deposit the fully subscribed share capital, and obtain the capital deposit certificate (شهادة إيداع رأس المال). The founders or their attorney then execute the Memorandum and Articles before the Notary Public; the notary authenticates signatures and annexes the deposited capital certificate to the instrument.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic (four originals)
Bank capital deposit certificate for the subscribed share capital
Founders' identity documents and residence proof
Power of Attorney for the incorporation agent
Source-of-funds / End-User Declaration for foreign capital remittances
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries signature discrepancies or missing annexes of the bank certificate, founders cure by reappearing at the notary office within 10 working days with corrected documents and pay the correction notary fee only.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporated Filing, Commercial Registry Certificate, and Gazette Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department – One-Stop Shop (incorporation windows and online investor services portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Memorandum, capital deposit certificate, name-clearance certificate, and GAFI application form electronically; GAFI verifies the package, issues the Commercial Registration certificate (شهادة القيد بالسجل التجاري) and tax-card pre-registration, and forwards the data for publication in the Official Bulletin. The company exists from the date of Commercial Registry entry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
GAFI incorporation application (electronic form)
Bank capital deposit certificate
Name clearance certificate
GAFI fee payment receipt and stamp duty receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner raises technical objections or requires additional capitalized-reserve wording, the incorporation agent files a formal rectification letter and corrected schedules within 15 days; contested fees or registry refusals may be appealed to the GAFI Grievance Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card, VAT Registration, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – District Tax Office and National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI / هيئة التأمينات الاجتماعية)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Commercial Registration certificate, submit the tax-card application (Form 1) to obtain the Unified Tax Number on a corporate-income-tax and VAT basis; register the legal representative and planned employees with NOSI within the statutory deadlines; initiate payroll withholding accounts. Keep separate files for the future manufacturing facility payroll.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Tax Card application Form 1 and bookmark form
VAT registration form (sales tax / general sales tax form for goods manufacturers)
Social Insurance registry Form 10 and employee declaration lists
Lease contract or proof of title to indicate the plant tax residence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late-registration penalties are mitigated by submitting a written statutory excuse and paying the nominal administrative fine within the cure period; the ETA may also correct tax-card data upon production of the final lease or plant address documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chamber of Commerce Membership and Municipal / Industrial-Zone Qualification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce and the local Governorate Municipality licensing office (plus SCZONE administration where the plant is inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for Chamber of Commerce membership using the commercial registration certificate; submit the factory lease contract or land title together with the mechanical and civil engineering drawings of the proposed CNC milling plant; obtain the preliminary municipality land-use / zoning certificate confirming the site may accommodate machine-tool manufacturing with coolant and metal processing operations.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate and tax card
Factory site lease contract / ownership title and cadastral extracts
Municipal building and zoning plan for the production hall
Chamber of Commerce membership application
SCZONE pre-approval if located within the Suez Canal Economic Zone
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the land-use certificate is refused because of industrial zone mismatch, the applicant re-submits with a corrected zone classification or applies to the governorate licensing committee for a change-of-use review; an administrative appeal lies to the Minister of Local Development.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Operating License Application to the Industrial Development Authority (IDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) – Industrial Licensing Center (single-window system established under Law No. 15 of 2017 and its Executive Regulation No. 958 of 2020)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete industrial licensing file through the IDA electronic portal, including the EEAA environmental approval, Civil Defense fire-safety certificate, detailed production-line technical specification of the five-axis CNC milling center manufacture (ISIC 2822), and the site civil-defense-approved drawings; IDA assesses within the legal review period and issues the Industrial Operating License (إجازة التشغيل الصناعي) allowing production to commence upon final inspection.
required_dossiers: IDA industrial license application and technical data sheet
Commercial Registration certificate and Unified Tax Number
EEAA Category B environmental approval
Civil Defense fire safety certificate for production halls
Site plan, mechanical layout, and building structural-load certificates
Technology file describing multi-axis CNC center subassembly, casting, and calibration operations
EOS (Egyptian Organization for Standardization and Quality) conformity plan for machine tools
Occupational safety and health record including noise, coolant mist, and VOC exposure measurements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IDA rejects the file or issues a correction list for site non-compliance or missing technical details, the applicant has a 15-day correction window to re-file; a second rejection may be appealed to the IDA Technical Licensing Committee within 30 days, and ultimately to the administrative courts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) – Industrial Licensing Center for the official manufacturing operating permit; the Egyptian Organization for Standardization and Quality (EOS) additionally issues product-conformity certification for CNC machine tools before first export.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License (إجازة التشغيل الصناعي) for the manufacture of multi-axis Computerized Numerical Control metal forming machine tools (ISIC 2822, NAICS 333517), issued under Law No. 15 of 2017 on Industrial Licensing and IDA Executive Regulation No. 958 of 2020

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Central Administration for Environmental Impact Assessment, Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (medium-impact facilities): saw-sheet step requiring submission of Form B screening with the project description and location; the facility will be elevated to Category C full Environmental Impact Assessment study if the cooling oil mist, VOC emissions, or metal dust loads exceed the threshold limits set in EEAA guidelines for engineering metal industry projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 (Environment Law, as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009) and Ministerial Decree 44 of 2000 (amended by Decrees 92 of 2013 and 69 of 2018): industrial wastewater to public sewer must meet pH 6–9.5, BOD5 ≤ 600 mg/L, COD ≤ 1100 mg/L, TSS ≤ 800 mg/L, and oil & grease ≤ 100 mg/L; metal machining coolants must be contained so that total heavy metals (Cr, Ni, Cd, Pb) remain below one-tenth of the listed maxima; stack and fugitive VOC capture with oil mist limited to 5 mg/m³ in the workplace atmosphere; hazardous residues (used metalworking fluids, metal swarf contaminated with emulsifiers) must be manifested, stored, transported, and disposed of in accordance with Article 27 of Law 4 of 1994 and EEAA industrial waste regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (خطاب الدفاع المدني) obtained from the General Administration of Civil Defense subcommittee of the Ministry of Interior, verifying fire-resistance ratings and escape routes for the production hall; structural-load inspection certificate covering the machine foundations, crane rails (if any), and vibration damping; Occupational Safety and Health clearance issued by the Ministry of Manpower, committing to workplace noise exposure of not more than 85 dB(A) over an 8-hour TWA, local-exhaust ventilation for coolant mist, machine-guarding systems, and chemical hygiene management for cutting fluids and lubricants.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory pre-operational clearance composed of: (1) Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate issued by the General Administration of Civil Defense under the Ministry of Interior for the manufacturing hall and storage areas; (2) structural-load and site-construction inspection certificates issued by an accredited engineering authority verifying floor loading capacity for the five-axis milling centers; and (3) Occupational Safety and Health workplace clearance issued by the Ministry of Manpower approving illuminated evacuation plans, fire alarms, coolant-mist extraction, machine guarding, PPE programmes, and medical surveillance files before IDA will activate the industrial operating license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – ETA e-Tax Portal (https://www.inatax.gov.eg/etax-web/)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident LLC must submit a complete registration application to ETA through an authorized tax agent or a duly appointed fiscal representative in Egypt. The application includes the commercial registry certificate (or foreign registration proof), constituent documents (AOA/BOA), board resolution appointing the Egyptian representative, power of attorney, and a statement of intended activities in Egypt. ETA issues a single 9-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN) for direct taxes, VAT, and payroll taxes. The same registration portal initiates VAT ID issuance simultaneously; failure to register within the prescribed period triggers penalty assessments and denial of input tax recovery.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide a US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election mechanism. Eligible manufacturing entities may, upon ETA/GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) approval, elect special tax regimes, including the Free Zone regime, the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) incentives, and the Investment Law 72/2017 incentive schemes. These elections are filings wholly within the standard entity-level taxation model and do not create flow-through status or hybrid mismatch positions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Egyptian Value Added Tax – Law No. 67 of 2016)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 (annual value of taxable supplies; foreign suppliers of services with Egyptian recipients may be subject to registration/reverse charge rules at the same threshold unless exempted by ETA directive)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: ETA’s e-invoicing system is mandatory for all registered taxpayers on a phased-basis. Taxpayers must transmit every B2B and B2G invoice to ETA’s central platform (Tax Electronic System) via an approved API or secure integration in near-real-time before issuance. ETA validates the invoice and returns a unique invoice identifier and QR code; no invoice may be legally issued without this digital clearance. The physical stamping regime is abolished, but non-integrated paper invoices are automatically treated as invalid for VAT deduction and subject the issuer to automatic blocking of the tax card.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported outside the customs territory of Egypt by a registered exporter, provided title in the goods passes to a non-resident buyer, the goods are removed from Egypt within the statutory period (normally 180 days from invoice/sale), and the export proceeds are credited to an Egyptian bank account within 180 days from the export date. The exporter must maintain digital and physical records evidencing the chain of movement (factory to customs to discharge from the vessel/aircraft) and corresponding foreign currency inflow.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (coded export entry released by Egyptian Customs Authority)
Bill of Lading (or Airway Bill) evidencing on-board loading at an Egyptian port/airport for foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank-issued certificate verifying receipt of export proceeds in freely convertible foreign currency)
Sales contract and pro-forma/commercial invoice issued to the non-resident buyer showing the applicable zero-rated status
ETA-approved export tax invoice bearing the e-invoicing validation QR code and the word 'Export'
Certificate of export value/transport manifest issued by the export customs office
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA audit teams automatically cross-match monthly export sales listings with customs release data, Egyptian bank SWIFT credit advices, and inward remittance certificates. If goods are not exported within 180 days, proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days, or documentation is false/incomplete, ETA retroactively assesses the standard 14% VAT on the full invoice value, adds late-payment interest (monthly delay fine), and denies input VAT refunds. Fraudulent claims constitute tax evasion under VAT Law 67/2016, leading to a fine of not less than EGP 20,000 and not more than EGP 100,000 or imprisonment (or both), confiscation of goods, and personal liability of directors and the appointed tax representative. Customs penalties and export privilege revocation also apply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — البنك المركزي المصري, operating under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) and its implementing prudential and foreign-exchange (FX) regulations issued through the Banking Supervision and Exchange Control Departments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Following the 6 March 2024 liberalization, Egypt maintains a market-determined flexible exchange rate regime consistent with IMF Extended Fund Facility commitments. Current-account transactions (trade in goods/services, royalties, management fees) are fully convertible and executable by CBE-licensed banks at prevailing interbank rates without pre-approval. Capital-account transactions, including foreign equity injection, intercompany loans, and profit/dividend repatriation, are permissible but require underlying-document verification under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (Articles 71–73 granting free transfer guarantees) and CBE unified FX rules. Practical remittance hurdles: all FX flows must pass through an Egyptian CBE-licensed bank (offshore transfers directly between non-resident accounts of the LLC are not recognized); the bank may require a valid tax clearance certificate and Corporate Tax ID for profit-transfer classification; and interbank liquidity conditions may temporarily delay large USD outflows, though no legal convertibility restriction exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the consolidated 2023–2024 CBE circulars on export proceeds, there is no mandatory conversion ratio: exporters may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign-currency accounts at an Egyptian bank, effectively abolishing prior surrender obligations. Export proceeds must be credited to the exporter's designated FCY account within 90 calendar days from the bill-of-lading/airway-bill date for open-account sales, or within the LC/documentary collection maturity schedule (maximum 1 year with documented CBE-bank approval). The collecting bank must record proceeds in the CBE Export Proceeds Monitoring System linked to customs (GUST/Sofacts) and the Export Development Fund; overdue non-repatriation constitutes a violation of Law No. 194 of 2020 Article 100 and may trigger suspension of export-financing facilities and enhanced compliance review of the entity's FX allocations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Alexandria S.A.E. (Intesa Sanpaolo Group)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut, Payoneer) cannot serve as primary treasury rails because they hold no Egyptian banking or exchange license; only CBE-licensed banks and licensed exchange bureaus may legally intermediate EGP transactions. The CBE Fintech Sandbox (Law No. 18 of 2019) offers an Egypt-incorporated EMI license for payment collection, but it does not confer FX dealing authorization and cannot settle EGP obligations on behalf of the LLC. EMIs are therefore limited to ancillary non-EGP disbursements to overseas contractors, subject to corporate tax withholding and full traceability in the statutory books.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is mandated for initial onboarding. Authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding 25% or more (or de facto control) must personally appear before the bank's Compliance and Remediation unit at an Egyptian branch. The CBE distance-KYC framework (November 2022) permits remote onboarding for retail consumers and low-risk limited companies only; an ISIC 2822 CNC manufacturer classified 'High_Risk_Special_License' is ineligible for remote acceptance. Where all shareholders are non-resident, the appointed managing director may attend under a notarized board resolution; corporate documents must be legalized by the Egyptian Consulate in the jurisdiction of incorporation (or apostilled for Hague Convention states); the compliance interview covers source of funds, expected FX volumes, counterparty list and physical asset location.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry segment flagged as high-risk dual-use machinery (multi-axis CNC with potential defence-component manufacturing applications)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI investment certificate; Ministry of Trade and Industry industrial registry license; Chamber of Engineering Industries membership; product catalogue restricted to ISIC 2822 (aerospace/automotive precision machining); internal trade-compliance policy with End-User/End-Use undertakings, denial-list screening protocol and no-military-aerospace customer covenant

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain containing Cyprus/UAE holding vehicles with opaque or layered ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial Registry extract issued within 3 months; notarized UBO declaration under Law No. 80 of 2002 (AMLR) Article 4; LLC constitutive contract (Law 159/1981 as amended) with certified Arabic translation; complete shareholder resolution chain evidencing control; audited financial statements supporting source of wealth

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign capital injection originating from FATF grey-listed jurisdictions or via non-bank money remitters
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Originating bank statement confirming the wire was sent from a licensed FATF-observant bank; equity contribution contract referencing GAFI registration; CBE FX declaration form (capital account notification); valid Tax ID card and corporate tax clearance; board resolution adopting a 'no third-party funds' policy

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value export contracts exceeding USD 1 million to MENA/African buyers with ambiguous end-use
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed export contract; commercial invoice cross-referenced to customs declaration; completed UNSCR 1540 and end-use questionnaires; serialized End-User Certificate for each CNC unit; purchaser's bank PO or finance-lease evidence; sanitized sanctions-screening report (Dow Jones / Refinitiv World-Check) delivered to the onboarding bank

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or PEP-linked minority shareholder involved in government procurement networks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: External-counsel Enhanced Due Diligence file; signed PEP status declaration; source-of-funds documentation for each PEP-linked contribution (sale contract, tax clearance, independent asset valuation); legal opinion confirming no government-contracting advantage within ISIC 2822 scope; threshold-based reporting protocol to the CBE Financial Intelligence Unit

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Irregular transaction profile: round-sum wires, urgent FX swaps, high-frequency CNC software license fees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy document with segregation of duties; licensed software and maintenance agreements (e.g., Siemens 840Dsl) explaining repeating fees; annual budgeted FX plan; e-invoicing (EFD) VAT codes matched to each transaction; quarterly reconciliation pack submitted to the relationship manager

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant sequence: (1) obtain GAFI investment certificate and Commercial Registry capitalization entry for EG_LLC; (2) open a dedicated capital escrow sub-account at NBE or CIB registered under the CBE capital-code framework; (3) execute the inbound wire via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own account with narrative 'STATUTORY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - EG_LLC - GAFI CERT NO. [X]'; (4) classify the flow in CBE Balance-of-Payments reporting as 'Direct Investment - Equity - Manufacturing' (CBE purpose code); (5) within 7 working days the CBE-licensed bank issues the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 Article 71 acknowledgment and capital certificate required for the Commercial Registry; (6) hold the injected funds in FCY or convert to EGP only upon documented treasury need; (7) maintain the complete KYC dossier (board resolution, notarized LLC deed, passport copies, source-of-funds bank statements) for CBE inspection. Any injection routed through a non-bank intermediary or lacking the GAFI certificate is reclassified as shareholder debt and triggers CBE net open position (NOP) reporting under Law 194 of 2020.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border settlements use three compliant clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for open-account imports of consumables and components (spindles, ball screws, controllers) with CBE import purpose codes and commercial invoice / VAT e-invoice cross-reference; (b) irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 under UCP 600 for high-value capital components (e.g., 5-axis heads from Japan, Switzerland or Germany), with settlement through MT103/MT202 and presentation documents conforming to the issuing bank's LC terms; (c) export receivables collected via documentary collections (D/P) or standby-LC-backed terms. The treasury desk executes daily sweeping of surplus FCY balances into CBE-licensed money market placements; all trade documentation must map to customs GUST/Sofacts declarations and the CBE Trade Monitoring portal, with bank charges and invoice rounding kept within tolerances.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP FX forwards — executed with CBE-licensed banks, maximum tenor 12 months, backed by documented trade or capital exposure and compliant with CBE derivative prudential rules
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — permissible only for the foreign parent to hedge offshore EGP exposure on non-repatriable local costs; the Egyptian entity itself may not execute offshore NDFs
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) — permitted to match USD-denominated CNC receivables against EGP local liquidity liabilities
Plain vanilla EUR/USD and USD/EGP FX options — permitted on a long-only (purchased) basis; writing of short options is prohibited except for covered monetization of surplus FCY
Dual-currency matched funding — structural FCY borrowing against USD inventory purchases, recognized as a CBE-eligible hedge reducing working-capital gap
Trade-finance forward overlay — confirmed EUR-denominated import LCs matched with EUR-denominated export receivables to neutralize EUR exposure at nil premium

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for legal persons (Egyptian Tax Form No. 11)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), competent tax office at the LLC's registered tax seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year LLC, on or before 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fixed penalty of EGP 2,000–20,000 plus additional tax of 5% per month or fraction thereof on unpaid tax per Law 91/2005; continued non-compliance triggers revocation of the tax card, bank attachment orders, and joint liability of managers for corporate tax debts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements, managers' report, auditor's report, and general assembly approval filed with the companies registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registry Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General assembly must approve the accounts within 90 days after fiscal year-end (by 31 March for a calendar-year LLC); the full audited package must be e-filed with GAFI within 30 days after approval (by 30 April)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 1,000–5,000 imposed on managers for non-filing under Law 159/1981; two consecutive years of default exposes the LLC to administrative strike-off from the Commercial Registry and judicial dissolution at the request of GAFI or any interested party.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) confirmation and shareholding status return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMCLU) through the GAFI unified corporate registry portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filled annually on the registration anniversary; any share transfer affecting a UBO with more than 25% direct or indirect interest must be filed within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Knowingly submitting false or incomplete UBO data is sanctionable under AML Law 174/2018 by imprisonment (up to one year) and/or a fine of up to EGP 1,000,000; directors and the legal representative are personally liable; the High-Risk Special License AML tier may additionally trigger enhanced due diligence and license review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the industrial operating license for the CNC five-axis milling center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local economic district authority or GAFI One-Stop-Shop for investment-licensed companies, with coordination file for Ministry of Trade and Industry (Industrial Registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Industrial operating license expires on 31 December of each calendar year; the complete renewal application must be submitted by 31 January of the following year to prevent interruption of operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a surcharge of 25%–50% of the annual license tariff and risk of administrative sealing of the factory premises; operating without a valid license is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of up to EGP 20,000 and a potential closure order.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit applies to every Egyptian LLC with no exemption based on capital, revenue, or headcount; Law 159/1981 requires the annual general assembly to appoint at least one auditor registered in the Ministry of Finance Accountants and Auditors Register under Law 133/1951. Free-zone manufacturers under Investment Law 72/2017 engaging exclusively in export activity may negotiate audit scope, but audited financial statements remain mandatory for CIT settlement and foreign-exchange reporting purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by Ministry of Finance Decree 110/2015 and subsequently updated; EAS is substantially converged with IFRS for business entities with limited local overrides, and all statutory filings, consolidated statements, and tax-basis financials must follow EAS presentation and disclosure requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO status attaches to any natural person owning or controlling, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the LLC's capital, voting rights, or appointment power over managers; the register of members must be updated for every share transfer, the transfer recorded in the share-transfer ledger, approved by the managers' resolution, and notarized when the memorandum of association is amended, with notification to GAFI and the Commercial Registry within 30 days. The annual UBO confirmation is submitted electronically through the GAFI portal together with the audited package; a nil-change declaration suffices in a year with no transfers, and a dormant LLC must still confirm its UBO data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders ledger with share-transfer annotations)
Register of Managers (directors) with appointments and signature specimens
Minute Book of the General Assembly and Managers' (Board) Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–900 per year for registered office address and local corporate agent services in Cairo or a major manufacturing zone; GAFI-licensed facilities with in-house secretariat tend toward the lower end
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–3,000 per year for a mid-sized CNC machine-tool manufacturing LLC; Big-4 and international-affiliate firms charge USD 4,000 and above and are not required under Egyptian GAAP practice for a private LLC.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72/2017 incentives: up to 50% deduction of investment cost for 7 years for eligible new industrial projects; 100% CIT exemption for qualifying free-zone and Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) manufacturing profits derived from exports; accelerated depreciation for CNC machine-tool assets; additional incentives for logistics and industrial integration projects under Ministerial Decree.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Income Tax Return Form No. 8 (Model 8) for limited liability companies, filed through the ETA unified e-filing portal (https://www.eta.gov.eg) with registered tax accountant PIN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with mandatory quarterly provisional CIT instalments (due within 30 days from the end of each quarter for companies) reconciled on the annual Form 8.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Form 8 must be filed within 4 months from the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by 30 April for a calendar-year LLC); audited financial statements and TP disclosure attachments are mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, tax card number, commercial registry number, address, and e-filing credentials.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the LLC's Egyptian tax card issued under Law 91/2005; for 100% foreign-owned LLCs, attach the parent company details and the Egyptian filing agent mandate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period: fiscal year start and end dates as stated in the articles of association.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned LLC may use a different fiscal year from its foreign parent; the chosen period must be registered with the ETA and the tax account opened accordingly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues: domestic sales of CNC five-axis milling centers, after-sales spare parts, calibration services, and export turnover.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export revenues in foreign currency must be recorded quarterly using the Central Bank average exchange rate; treaty export commission arrangements must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: imported CKD components, locally sourced castings, direct machining labor, and factory overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany import prices from the foreign parent must be benchmarked at arm's length; attach import invoices and customs declarations for ETA TP review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: salaries, rent, utilities, maintenance, quality-control consumables, and end-user installation costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses allocated from the foreign head office (management fees) are deductible only if real services are rendered, documented, and within the TP guidelines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business profit or loss before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed under Egyptian GAAP; non-resident-owned LLCs must not deduct head-office notional interest or imputed royalties without ETA approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and disallowed expenses: penalties, donations exceeding statutory limits, overstated depreciation, and disallowed head-office costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallowed head-office overhead and foreign taxes paid by the parent are non-deductible; adjust accordingly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment incentives: free-zone exemption, Investment Law 72/2017 deductions, and accelerated depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only substantive SCZone/free-zone manufacturers with export documentation may claim the exemption; letterbox LLCs are ineligible and face full taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilized: up to 5-year carryforward of statutory tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the foreign parent or affiliated permanent establishment cannot be transferred; only the Egyptian LLC's own audited losses may be carried forward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and tax computation at the 22.5% statutory rate after deductions and exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are subject to a final 10% dividend WHT on distributions from after-tax retained earnings; the LLC files as withholding agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: quarterly provisional instalments, foreign tax credit, and previous overpayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is available for Egyptian LLC profits taxed abroad only under a DTA and upon submission of a notarized residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund claimed, including withholding taxes suffered on Egyptian-sourced income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Final balance must be settled electronically; refund claims by non-residents are processed through the ETA refund committee and may be offset against outstanding WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions and TP disclosure: aggregate value of controlled transactions, selected OECD method, and place of TP file retention.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned LLCs must attach the ETA TP disclosure concerning the foreign parent, including CUP/TNMM benchmarks prepared for the Egyptian entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of 10% of tax assessed (minimum EGP 5,000 for medium and large taxpayers) plus a 2% monthly delay surcharge on the unpaid tax; late payment: surcharge of 2% per month on the outstanding balance; non-filing: criminal fine of EGP 20,000-100,000 and imprisonment for persistent default; inaccurate filing: 20% administrative penalty on the tax under-declared.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders (Law No. 91/2005, Articles 7 and 56); resident corporate recipients are exempt where the distributing profits have already borne Egyptian CIT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced DTA withholding rates: (1) confirm the DTA between Egypt and the shareholder's residence state is in force; (2) obtain the residence state Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) for the relevant year; (3) submit to the ETA or the withholding LLC before payment the TRC, a beneficial ownership declaration in the form prescribed by the ETA, and evidence of the shareholding percentage if seeking a reduced rate for substantial holdings; (4) obtain the ETA treaty clearance endorsement before remittance; if excess WHT is withheld at source, file a refund claim within 5 years from the payment date with the original TRC and payment vouchers.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on non-resident royalties: 20%; statutory WHT on non-resident interest: 20%; typical DTA relief: 10-15% on interest and 8-12% on royalties depending on the treaty partner; royalties embedded in imported CNC control software must be apportioned and separately sourced for WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 aggregate value of controlled transactions in a fiscal year; above this threshold, the Egyptian LLC must prepare and submit on ETA demand a BEPS-aligned Local File and Master File (Egyptian TP Guidelines, Decree No. 652 of 2020); a CbCR is required for MNE groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 900 million where Egypt hosts a constituent entity.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not enacted UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the ETA applies OECD BEPS substance-over-form and beneficial ownership doctrines. A non-resident-owned LLC must demonstrate real premises, technical staff, machining operations, and export activities to claim free-zone/SCZone exemptions or DTA relief. Shell holding vehicles and letterbox LLCs distributing profits without substance are recast as Egyptian tax residents with denial of treaty WHT benefits and risk of liquidation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating dual accounting ledgers, deliberately understating export proceeds from CNC milling center sales, inflating imported raw-material costs through shell suppliers, or backdating board resolutions to obscure taxable years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 3-5 years and fine of EGP 10,000-100,000 under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 (Articles 133-134); reassessment on deemed turnover at 22.5%; 2% monthly delay surcharge; 20% administrative penalty on under-declared tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax; ETA may issue asset freezes, seize passports, impose travel bans, and refer the case to the Economic Criminal Court with direct criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and submit the Local File/Master File despite controlled transactions above EGP 10,000,000; applying a non-approvable method; selecting a loss-making local distributor comparable; or submitting falsified benchmark sets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Specific penalty up to EGP 100,000 and disallowance of related-party deductions; the ETA may replace the transaction price via TNMM/CUP and impose 2% monthly surcharge on the adjustment, with a 20% penalty on the underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-arm's length intercompany contracts are jointly liable for the upward adjustment; personal bank accounts may be attached, and deliberate submission of doctored comparables triggers criminal sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Channeling Egyptian CNC manufacturing profits through a zero-substance Cayman or BVI holding company and declaring dividends to claim reduced 5-10% DTA WHT or free-zone exemption without real personnel, premises, or operational decision-making in Egypt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits; re-characterization of the holding vehicle as a sham; full 22.5% CIT on undistributed profits, 10% final dividend WHT without treaty relief, administrative fines up to EGP 1,000,000 under anti-avoidance rules, and compulsory liquidation or strike-off of the Egyptian LLC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who sign substance certificates or shell board minutes bear civil liability for recaptured taxes; travel bans and passport seizure; exclusion from holding directorships in Egypt; referral for penal sanction under Companies Law No. 159/1981.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Export Control Red Flags in Trade-Based Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting payments for multi-axis CNC centers via unverified third-party cryptocurrency exchanges or layered Swift wires from OFAC/UN-sanctioned end-users; submitting falsified End-User Certificates to disguise the ultimate destination of dual-use precision machine tools; cash settlement above statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under AML Law No. 80/2002: fines up to EGP 500,000 and imprisonment of 1-7 years; freezing of corporate and personal accounts; revocation of the statutory export license and cross-border trade license; forfeiture of shipments and denial of future End-User Certificate LC rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for failures to file Suspicious Transaction Reports with the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU); personal asset seizure, travel bans, and imprisonment for systematic money laundering or dual-use export violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying royalties or interest to a non-resident technology licensor/shareholder without the statutory 20% WHT, remitting dividends to foreign shareholders without 10% WHT, or claiming DTA reduced rates without a TRC and beneficial ownership proof.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The LLC remains liable for the unwithheld tax plus 2% monthly surcharge and a 20% penalty on the deficient WHT; ETA denial of operational expense deductions for unwithheld royalties; criminal fine of EGP 10,000-40,000 for repeated failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors acting as withholding agents are personally and jointly liable for the unwithheld amounts; the ETA can enforce against personal bank accounts, issue a travel ban, and the Economic Court may impose imprisonment of up to one year for willful non-remittance.
